notes.emmwanyi: The crop. A cup of coffee is kaawa.

guidebook.intro: Most Baganda have roots in a village garden, with matooke, coffee and groundnuts growing side by side.

tips.title: Doing it for someone: -ir- / -er-
body: Add **-ir-** or **-er-** before the last vowel to say “for”, “to” or “at”: **-lima** (dig) becomes **-limira** (dig for), **-fumba** becomes **-fumbira** (cook for), **-tunda** becomes **-tundira** (sell at).
Verbs with **e** or **o** in the stem usually take **-er-**: **-kola** becomes **-kolera** (work for), as in **Nkolera kampuni** from Unit 14.

culture.title: The banana garden
body: The **olusuku** (banana garden) is the centre of a Ganda homestead. Matooke grows all year round, and a well-kept olusuku was a sign of a good household.
